foot.not_advice: It is not medical advice. It cannot diagnose, and nothing here should start, stop or change a medicine or a care plan without your own prescriber or care team; stopping an antidepressant suddenly can cause discontinuation symptoms. The PHQ-9, the EPDS, the criteria counter and the other scales are teaching tools that show how clinicians score them, never a self-test or a diagnosis. Doses, tapering schedules, thresholds and guideline statements are quoted as published in drug labels and by the APA, CANMAT, NICE, the ACP and the VA/DoD, never as instructions, and trial results are group averages, not predictions for any person. If you are in crisis or thinking about suicide, contact local emergency services or a crisis line (in the US call or text 988; in the UK and Ireland Samaritans 116 123). Please check the original sources, which are listed in full in the Sources module.
shell.disclaimer: The Depression Companion is an educational synthesis of published literature for study and understanding. Depression is a common, treatable illness, not weakness. The guide does not replace a doctor, psychiatrist, psychologist, nurse or pharmacist. The PHQ-9, the criteria counter and the other scales are teaching aids, not self-tests, and doses and schedules are quoted as published, never as instructions: do not start, stop or change a medicine without your prescriber. Trial results are group averages, not predictions for any person. If you are in crisis or thinking about suicide, contact local emergency services or a crisis line (in the US call or text 988; in the UK and Ireland Samaritans 116 123).
shell.note: An animated, cited guide for students, people living with depression, and their families and caregivers. Educational only, not medical advice. Your place is saved on this device.
